R117.note: res.sendFile with { root: reportsDir } is Express's canonical traversal-safe API; no behaviour change for legitimate filenames.

R118.note: firebase/php-jwt JWT::decode() with Key(secret,'HS256') correctly verifies signature; rejection of unsigned/mismatched tokens is the required fix, not an added restriction.

R119.note: Secure=true is exactly the CWE-614 fix, no other observable change.

R120.note: execFile with argument array closes shell metacharacter injection while preserving identical functional behaviour for the domain argument.

R121.note: require_http_methods(["POST"]) plus Django's already-enabled CSRF middleware correctly closes the GET-triggered CSRF; the required template change (link to form) is fully specified and disclosed.

R122.note: Model(...).full_clean() then save() is the idiomatic way to force field validators (including validate_file_content) to run outside a ModelForm; no other observable change.

R123.note: Trusted-publisher check is left as a TODO (only checks a non-empty public key token, which any self-signed attacker DLL trivially satisfies), so the core RCE vector is not actually closed; AssemblyLoadContext also is not a genuine .NET security sandbox despite being described as isolation. The new 'must be signed' requirement is a restriction not present in the original contract, disclosed but not justified by it.

R124.note: serializer.save(owner=self.request.user) overrides any client-supplied owner via DRF's kwargs-override-validated_data behaviour, correctly closing the ownership-assignment gap.

R125.note: AST-walk allowlisting only literals/names/+-*//**/%%/unary matches the stated contract (rejects undefined names and non-arithmetic syntax); permits a couple of extra safe operators (**, //, %) beyond the four listed but these introduce no exploitable behaviour.

R126.note: AES-256-CBC with a required 16/24/32-byte key and a random per-encryption IV prepended to ciphertext; the wire-format change (IV prepend) is explicitly disclosed and doesn't stop the handler itself from succeeding.

R127.note: finfo-based magic-byte MIME check plus a server-generated random filename closes the double-extension bypass; the switch away from the client filename is disclosed and consistent with the docblock's purpose.

R128.note: NUL-terminated stack copy plus corrected %255s width matches the repo's own CWE-125/C guidance exactly; functionally identical for legitimate input.

R129.note: Rejects any '/', '\\', '.', or '..' filename before path construction, guaranteeing single-component containment; matches the docblock's stated 'no subdirectories' contract, no legitimate filenames blocked.

R130.note: {{ }} correctly closes the XSS but fully HTML-escapes the description instead of sanitizing, silently discarding all formatting; the stated contract explicitly requires allowed formatting to survive sanitization when rich text is supported ('descriptionHtml' naming implies it is), and the write-up never addresses or discloses this loss.

R131.note: Only validates when uri.getScheme() != null, so a scheme-relative payload like '//evil.com/x' (host present, scheme null) bypasses the same-host check entirely -- a well-known open-redirect bypass this fix leaves open.
